product.name: dbSDK
product.tagline: Create, manage, and query databases with one TypeScript SDK
product.scope: Management (control plane), the typed PostgreSQL query client, one-way resumable sync between databases (dbsdk/sync), and optional Drizzle ORM interoperability (dbsdk/drizzle). Bring a provider credential (Supabase PAT, Neon API key, PlanetScale service token); there is no central dbSDK backend.

adapters.notes: Mandatory verified TLS on remote hosts (system trust store); connection-string SSL directives are canonicalized and stripped so pg cannot override the resolved policy; the only downgrade path is an explicit ssl:{rejectUnauthorized:false} option, and remote plaintext is refused. connectionMode must match the endpoint port (direct 5432, PgBouncer pooled 6432); mismatches are refused unless allowModeMismatch. Localhost defaults to no TLS. Only PlanetScale Postgres: Vitess/MySQL and Neki are separate systems.
adapters.evidence: flags: docs; behavior additionally verified against a real local server (wire protocol, TLS config resolution, pooled guards)

capabilities.pagination: projects and branches paginate; the database list does not
capabilities.listScope: branch lists require projectId on the query; database lists require projectId and branchId (typed on ManagementListQuery); role lists require projectId and branchId scope

managementAdapters.notes: Databases are branch-scoped and addressed by name. Provider-defined kinds: role (branch-scoped Postgres credentials; no update — the official API has no role PATCH), endpoint (branch compute; create requires branchId and type; start/suspend/restart actions), snapshot (no single GET in the official API; restore returns the restored branch). Create responses carry connection URIs and role passwords; they surface only via secrets and are redacted from raw payloads. connection() requires caller-supplied databaseName and roleName (official endpoint requirement); URI password redacted unless reveal: true. raw.connectionUri and raw.revealRolePassword honor reveal and register revealed secrets for later error redaction. raw.recoverProject restores a deleted project. regions() forwards a supplied organizationId as org_id (optional; recommended by Neon for accurate availability). wait() on a bare project or database ref is refused with CAPABILITY (no status field); pass the write result or operation.
managementAdapters.evidence: docs (official Neon API v2); behavior covered by recorded-HTTP tests

create:project: db_pass (required by the API; generated when password is omitted)

managementAdapters.notes: A Supabase project is the PostgreSQL database; creating kind 'database' is refused with CAPABILITY. The API never echoes db_pass; when password is omitted the adapter generates one and returns it once via secrets. resetCredential rotates the project password (official PATCH, generated when omitted). action(project,'resume') is the un-pause primitive: official POST /v1/projects/{ref}/restore (the dashboard's Resume project button, projects:write scope); the endpoint echoes no resource or operation, so wait() on the action result is refused by design — poll get() instead. action(branch,'restore') cancels a scheduled branch deletion (not point-in-time data restore; backups/PITR is an unimplemented gap). No recover-deleted-project endpoint exists. Current-API facts: a spec plan is refused with CONFIGURATION (plans are chosen at the organization level), a spec region maps to the official region_selection form, and organization_id is deprecated-but-accepted alongside providerOptions.organization_slug. wait() polls resource status because there is no operations endpoint. Connection bridge: connection() exposes the official host for a direct project connection (the payload carries no database/role fields) and pooler details via the official pooler config endpoint; the SDK never fabricates a URL from the token.
managementAdapters.evidence: docs (official Supabase Management API v1 spec, plus official dashboard source for resume semantics); behavior covered by recorded-HTTP tests

managementAdapters.credential: PlanetScale service token (tokenId + tokenSecret; Authorization: <id>:<secret>, no Bearer scheme)

capabilities.pagination: page-based on all implemented list endpoints (page/per_page); a limit above the official maximum of 100 is refused before dispatch
capabilities.listScope: branch lists require projectId (the database name slug); role lists require projectId and branchId scope

managementAdapters.notes: PlanetScale's database (the managed, billable unit) maps to kind 'project'; branches map to 'branch' with projectId = the database NAME SLUG; Postgres role credentials are the provider-defined 'role' kind, scoped {projectId, branchId} and addressed by uid (name is a separate field; databases/branches are name-addressed). All CRUD is organization-scoped: the factory organization is the required owner, including create('project'); a mismatching spec.organizationId is refused with zero dispatch. Discovery (organizations(), regions(), raw.clusterSizeSkus()) may target other orgs explicitly. Engine gate: every mutating verb first GETs the parent database (official kind field, never cached) and refuses non-PostgreSQL parents BEFORE the mutation; a missing kind fails honestly (PROVIDER), and list('project') filters mixed-engine pages. create('project') takes no plan field and no create-time password — credentials come from roles. raw.clusterSizeSkus always sends engine=postgresql (official default is mysql) and returns the official array UNFILTERED (enabled:false included). Role passwords are ONE-TIME secrets (create/reset): they surface only in secrets, are redacted from raw, and are registered for later error redaction; connection() never fabricates a password and its URI is always redacted. resetCredential(role) rotates server-generated (caller passwords refused, zero requests); raw.renewRole extends a role's expiration without a new password. No operations API: wait() polls the resource's own readiness (role readiness precedence: dropped/deleted -> deleting, expired/disabled -> paused, then ready). Refused rather than guessed (official endpoints exist, unverified this round): branch update (PATCH), backups/restore, deploy requests, IP restrictions, bouncers, and all lifecycle actions (declared actions: none). Vitess/MySQL and Neki are separate systems, not modeled.
managementAdapters.evidence: docs (official PlanetScale API per-endpoint references); behavior covered by injected-HTTP tests and real local-PG driver legs; no hosted PlanetScale endpoint exercised
